A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same distributions-as-actions research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–H support reliable comparison, including matching material across changed page breaks.

before.justification: v2 reports original DA-AC evaluations across continuous, discrete, and hybrid control, plus bandit experiments and ICL ablations (Section 5; Appendices D and F).

after.justification: v3 retains original benchmark evaluations, bandit experiments, and ablation results in Section 5 and Appendices D and F.

M1.justification: The DA-MDP formulation, DA-PG estimator, ICL update, and TD3-based DA-AC procedure are unchanged, including policy parameterizations and Appendix G pseudocode.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same bandits, MuJoCo/DMC continuous and discretized-control tasks, Gym classic control, MinAtar, and seven hybrid PAMDP environments (Section 5; Appendices D and F).

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within the continuous, discrete, high-dimensional discrete, hybrid, and bandit experiments. This includes TD3/RP-AC/SAC/PPO for continuous control and PATD3/PDQN/HHQN for hybrid control. The new citations introduce no evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Training budgets, seven-bin action discretization, return normalization, hybrid evaluation procedures, and model configurations remain unchanged in Section 5 and Appendices D–E.

E4.justification: Both retain the same ICL ablations, bandit critic and gradient analyses, learning-rate comparisons, actor-target-network analysis, and continuous-versus-discretized action comparison (Figures 7–12).

E5.justification: Both report 10 seeds for control experiments, 50 for bandit policy optimization, 95% bootstrap confidence intervals with 10,000 resamples, and the same paired t-test procedures in Appendix D.8.

E6.justification: Experimental plots and result entries are unchanged, including Appendix F learning curves. Table 1 retains the across-settings ICL mean difference of 0.0508, t = 3.820, and p = 0.0088.

T1.justification: Definitions, assumptions, theoretical results, and mathematical arguments are retained. Appendix C.2 shortens the closing sentence of Proposition 4.3's proof while preserving the same DA-PG/DPG equality; this is an equivalent restatement.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about the distributions-as-actions framework, lower-variance gradients, ICL, and competitive DA-AC performance across action types.

C2.justification: The critic approximation bias discussion, ICL's omitted importance-weight corrections, bandit interpretations, and limitations concerning discrete-action structure are unchanged. The new related-work paragraph changes positioning rather than these interpretations or limitations.

D1.justification: Code-access information, implementation details, policy parameterizations, hyperparameter tables, computational-resource disclosures, and pseudocode remain unchanged (reproducibility statement; Appendices D, E, and G).

R1.justification: Appendix A adds an agent–environment-boundary paragraph citing Jiang (2019), Harutyunyan (2020), and Abel et al. (2025), with corresponding bibliography entries. It distinguishes their perspectives from this paper's action-space shift and algorithmic focus, providing a limited positioning expansion.

P1.justification: v3 adds one short related-work paragraph and makes the conclusion of Proposition 4.3's proof more concise. The main narrative and section ordering remain stable.

P2.justification: The bibliography and early appendices reflow, changing paragraph and equation placement across page breaks. Section 4.3 italicizes 'importance sampling.' Figures, table designs, and captions are unchanged.

improvement.justification: v3 addresses a small contextual omission by acknowledging additional work on agent–environment boundaries and explaining the paper's distinct action-space focus in Appendix A. This improves attribution and positioning. The methods, theoretical substance, empirical evidence, and reproducibility information remain unchanged, so the overall gain is limited.
